question: The exercise works from site allele frequency likelihoods (SAF) rather than called genotypes. Why does that matter for the SFS in particular?

answers.answer: Calling genotypes at low depth systematically loses heterozygotes and rare alleles, which distorts exactly the low-frequency end of the SFS the statistics read
answers.feedback: Correct — this is the reason for the whole approach.

answers.answer: It makes no difference, only speed

question: Fst is computed for a pair of populations. What does PBS add?

answers.answer: It splits three pairwise Fst values into a branch length per population, so you can say which population the differentiation belongs to
It is a normalised version of Fst

answers.feedback: It does not give a p-value.

question: A locus has high Fst between CEU and YRI. Why is that alone weak evidence of selection?

answers.answer: Drift produces high-Fst loci by chance, so a scan needs the rest of the genome as a comparison and still only gives outliers, not proof
Fst cannot detect selection at all
answers.feedback: It can, as an outlier scan.

answers.answer: Only haplotype methods can detect selection

question: The 2D SFS is estimated for a pair of populations. What is it used for here?

answers.answer: It is the input for the Fst estimator — Fst is computed from the joint frequency spectrum
